contamination_note: The query string matches any certificate name containing '.onion', so it returns certificates for clearnet domains such as 'onion--markets.com' and 'kraken-onion--link.info' as well as real onion addresses. Only entries carrying a well-formed v2 or v3 .onion SAN are counted here; the remainder is reported rather than dropped.
interpretation: Real certificates show the vendor-default collision as it exists in the wild: the single most common issuer covers a large share of all onion-bearing certificates (59.2%). A correlator that links services sharing an issuer would merge that entire share into one operator. This is the same failure the synthetic farm measures, observed on real data. Separately, only 2 clearnet names co-occur with an onion address across these certificates, which is the minority-signal claim about Certificate Transparency measured rather than asserted.
